title: serving-runtime-daily-scratchpad-2026-04-01
content:
Quick notes (working):

Date: 2026-04-01
Owner: Ava M.

Priority/Context:
- Follow-up on the regressed p95 latency flagged yesterday on g4dn clusters. Appears when seq_len > 2048 and batching kicks in.
- Triage ticket SRV-1234: intermittent spikes during caching warm-up.

Top of mind TODOs:
- [ ] Reproduce p95 regression locally with small-ish workload (deadline: 4/2) -- use perf harness with seq_len sampling set to 512/1024/2048/4096. (Ravi helping)
- [ ] Add extra logging around KV cache hit/miss and batch formation (short-term).
- [ ] Patch: limit batch size for long seqs as temp mitigation (PR draft WIP, see PR #842).
- [ ] Run canary with kernel-optimizations branch on dedicated pool (2-hour window).
- [ ] Draft post-mortem skeleton if issue persists > 24h.

Investigation notes:
- Observed behavior: throughput steady but p95 jumps ~2x when sequence length mix shifts to >2048 for ~5-10% of requests. CPU on host not saturated; GPU utilisation drops suggesting stalls.
- Hypothesis A: dynamic kernel selection path introduces a slow path for long sequences when combined with continuous batching (path picks different kernel and triggers CUDA stream sync).
- Hypothesis B: KV cache eviction/reload for long contexts happens mid-batch causing rework and stalls.

Commands/experiments to run:
- ./perf/harness --model redwood-3b --seq-len 512,1024,2048,4096 --qps 50 --batch-policy adaptive 
  -> capture NVTX, GPU timeline, and host thread dumps
- enable debug env: RW_LOG_KV_CACHE=debug RW_BATCH_DEBUG=1 RW_KERNEL_TRACE=1 (short run)

Kernel notes:
- kernel-selector: currently favors fused-attn kernel for seq<=2048, falls back to chunked-attn for >2048. Need to verify fallback is not forcing a sync.
- Check kernel wrapper: ensure it uses async launches and doesn't call cudaDeviceSynchronize in error path.
- Look for memcpy host->device in hot path during cache refill. If present, move to pinned memory + async copy.

Quick code pointers:
- suspect files: runtime/kernel_selector.cpp, runtime/kv_cache_manager.cpp, runtime/batching/scheduler.cpp
- grep TODOs: git grep "TODO: sync" runtime || true

Notes from logs (raw snippets):
- "WARN batch.cpp: batch_flush  pid=... elapsed_ms=1234 seq_mean=2580 cache_miss=0.12"
- "TRACE kernel_selector.cpp: selected=chunked_attn reason=seq_len>2048 est_ms=12 actual_ms=85"

Short-term mitigations to push to canary:
- Limit max_batch_size for >2048 sequences to 4 (config override).
- Add backoff when cache miss rate > 0.1 to avoid repeated refetch storms.

Meetings / coordination:
- 10:30am sync with SRE (Maya) to grab host metrics and eBPF traces for the timeframe.
- 3:00pm triage with kernel team (Ravi, Jonas) to review NVTX and kernel traces. Bring PR #842 draft.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Does the model compile step pick different kernels based on dynamic shape heuristics at runtime, or only on static config? Need clarity from compilation path owner (Jonas).
- Edge case: are we invalidating cache when sequence length increases mid-conversation? That would explain large device-to-host traffic.

Micro-tasks (15-60m):
- [ ] Add perf counters for kernel selection reasons (file + line) -- 30m
- [ ] Add cache hit/miss percentile logging (p50/p90/p99) in kv_cache_manager -- 45m
- [ ] Smoke test PR #842 on staging with synthetic workload (15m + 30m run)

Backlog items (post-mitigation):
- Improve kernel autotuner: model/seq-aware latency estimator instead of simple thresholds.
- Rework cache refill protocol to batch evictions + prefetch to avoid mid-batch misses.
- Explore quantization-optimized kernels for long sequences to reduce memory pressure.

Links / refs:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842
- Ticket: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/SRV-1234
- Design note: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRV/kv-cache-design

Notes-to-self:
- Keep triage doc short. Focus on reproducible artifacts (commands, NVTX, timeline screenshots).
- If we can't repro within 4 hours, escalate to on-call for live-capture window.

End of scratchpad.
